From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zenworks order form + DPA: redlines attached and next steps

Emma — thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, attaching the latest Order Form (v3) and our baseline DPA for your legal review. A few quick asks so we can keep procurement moving: 

- Please confirm whether you view Redwood as "processor" for the integration work or if you need us to accept controller-level obligations for any portion (we flagged the areas in the attached doc).
- Highlight any SCCs (or jurisdictional) concerns in the attached PDF redline — we saw specific objections around the US-hosting clause and KMS key control language.
- If you want to propose an alternate Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) language, send that back; otherwise we can draft TIA text that limits transfers to approved subprocessors and adds supplemental safeguards.

Timeline: procurement needs an executed order form + DPA by Oct 15 to make the Q4 onboarding window. If that's tight, tell us which items we should escalate for legal exec sign-off vs. which can be operational mitigations.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Emma Smith <emma.smith@zenworks.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Zenworks Legal <legal@zenworks.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 11:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Zenworks order form + DPA: redlines attached and next steps

Ben — thanks, attaching our commentary. High level: Zenworks legal can't accept the base DPA as-is (see attachments). Main concerns: 

1) Cross-border transfers: the SCCs appendix you provided doesn't reflect the UK addendum variants we require; we'd prefer a Transfer Impact Addendum that enumerates safeguards for transfers to US regions, or alternatively a contractual commitment to only use subprocessors who have EU/UK adequacy or binding instruments.
2) Controller vs Processor: we need explicit carveouts for controller obligations tied to customer data we ingest for analytics. If Redwood will be performing analytics on aggregated customer data, we need a section limiting reuse and ensuring data minimization.
3) KMS/Key custody: Zenworks must retain control of KMS keys for any customer encrypted datasets (we can accept a technical integration but keys must be held in our tenant/HSM).

We attached: zenworks_sccs_redline.pdf (SCCs + TIA suggestion) and a one-page gap matrix summarizing evidence we need (SOC 2 Type II, encryption-at-rest details, subprocessor list).

We can be flexible on some order form commercial terms but the privacy clauses are non-negotiable for our security steering committee — they want evidence rather than promises.

Emma
Emma Smith
Sr. Contracts Manager, Zenworks
emma.smith@zenworks.com

Attachments: zenworks_sccs_redline.pdf, zenworks_gap_matrix.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Zenworks order form + DPA: redlines attached and next steps

Soojin / Ben — reviewed Zenworks' attachments and ran a quick gap analysis. See summary and recommended negotiation positions below. I attached a redlined order form and a short gap matrix (zenworks_gap_matrix.xlsx) to support procurement's ask.

Executive summary (3 bullets):
- Cross-border transfers / SCCs: Zenworks is asking for UK-specific SCC language and a Transfer Impact Addendum. We should offer a two-track approach: (A) Accept SCCs + our supplemental TIA language that documents technical and organisational safeguards (preferred), or (B) allow Zenworks to propose their TIA if they both accept a limited acceptance window (90 days) for new subprocessors and allow audits. Track A keeps us in control of the language and avoids full controller commitments.

- KMS/Key custody: we cannot accept full handover of keys for production inference workloads because of shared-running architectural constraints. We can offer a tenant-isolation model for customer-specific encryption keys (customer-managed keys via our KMS integration) for data at rest and limit Redwood's access via HSM-backed envelopes. If Zenworks insists on sole custody, escalate to the platform team + execs — that is a higher-cost operational change and we should reserve it for enterprise pricing commitments.

- Controller vs Processor and analytics reuse: propose a narrow clause that allows aggregate/anonymous telemetry for improving model performance but prohibits using customer-identifiable data for model training or product features without separate opt-in. This is a typical compromise and addresses Zenworks' data-minimization concern.

Actionable next steps: 
1) Ben: send Zenworks a short email proposing Track A language and include our redlined DPA excerpt for SCCs + TIA (I attached zenworks_orderform_v3_redline.docx with inline DPA suggestions). Ask whether they will accept our evidence package in place of contract concessions: SOC 2 Type II, encryption architecture doc, subprocessor roster and penalty language for unauthorized transfers.
2) Soojin: if Zenworks pushes hard on key custody, we need a call between Platform (product infra lead), Legal (me) and Zenworks security to scope feasibility and cost. If that's needed, mark as "exec escalation" and give a cost estimate.
3) Laura will prepare an internal decision log to record items we concede vs. escalate (I will update the gap matrix and add negotiation fallback language).

Suggested language snippets (short):
- SCCs/TIA: "Supplier shall process Transfers only under SCCs executed by the parties, supplemented by the Transfer Impact Addendum attached as Schedule X; Supplier shall implement the administrative and technical safeguards described in Schedule X and provide the Controller with the evidence set described in Section Y."
- KMS: "Customer may elect customer-managed encryption keys via the Supplier's supported KMS integrations; where elected, Supplier shall not persist plaintext keys and shall log administrative access to keys subject to audit."
- Analytics reuse: "Supplier may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for model improvement provided such data cannot reasonably be re-identified and not used to target or profile Controller's end users without explicit prior written consent."

I attached: zenworks_orderform_v3_redline.docx (order form with inline redlines), zenworks_gap_matrix.xlsx (evidence checklist). Ben — if you can send the Track A proposal today we can try to close before Oct 15.

Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
